extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and summarizing developments in an international diplomatic/military crisis, using official texts, statements, and on-the-ground color to inform readers of positions, reactions, and likely consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include text of U.S. and German notes / official decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of U.S. and German Notes On Absorption of Czech State; verbatim excerpts of the March 16 decree and the U.S. reply are reproduced (e.g., 'The Government of the United States does not recognize that any legal basis exists for the status so indicated.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish full or extended verbatim texts of official notes and decrees (with dates and signatories) to let readers see primary-source language; label clearly (e.g., 'Text of... follows'); include relevant article numbers (Article 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13) from decrees when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report official legal recognition/status
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state government positions on recognition (example wording used: 'The Government of the United States does not recognize that any legal basis exists for the status so indicated.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote or paraphrase the exact legal position of governments regarding sovereignty/recognition; explain what recognition (or lack of it) implies diplomatically and legally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute statements to named officials with titles and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes and paraphrases are attributed to named officials and offices (e.g., 'Acting Secretary of State Welles', 'Lord Halifax', 'President Lebrun', 'Secretary Morgenthau').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always give the official's name, title, and, where relevant, the occasion or dateline; note when a statement repeats or clarifies an earlier public remark (e.g., 'repeated his statement of yesterday').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear datelines and wire-service credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections begin with datelines and wire-service tags (e.g., 'WASHINGTON, March 21 (A.P.)', 'LONDON, March 21 (A.P.).').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start dispatches with city and date; include wire-service attribution to indicate sourcing and to permit readers to place the report; separate multiple datelined sections when covering different capitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a chronological timeline of key events and dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece ties actions to dates and sequences (March 16 decree; March 17 German note; March 20/21 releases; references to prior events like Sept. 29 Munich).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List or weave in key dates and the order of events so readers can follow cause-effect and timing; when reproducing official texts, clearly indicate the date they were issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize international reactions and consultation status
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports which governments have reacted or been consulted (e.g., 'No Word Yet From Britain', 'no exchange of views had taken place between this and any other Government', 'Brazil and Chile were making soundings').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which states have been consulted, which have declined or delayed comment, and any reported diplomatic démarches or 'soundings'; make explicit when there has been 'no exchange' or 'no comment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain fiscal and economic effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage includes economic ramifications: treasury stock levels, a Commerce Department memorandum on German finances, commodity index levels, concerns about influx of gold, and Reich labor shortages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sourced economic indicators and official comment (names/titles) tying political developments to fiscal/market effects; quantify impacts where possible and note official assessments or denials (e.g., Morgenthau's remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail domestic legislative and policy responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Article reports proposed or enacted legislative measures and policy proposals (U.S. neutrality legislation and Pittman cash-and-carry bill; British bill to postpone payments from certain Czecho-Slovakian accounts; French decrees altering labor hours and mobilization powers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name bills/decrees, sponsors or issuing authorities, and summarize their key provisions and intended effect; indicate timetables (e.g., 'will be given to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee tomorrow').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report military and mobilization measures precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of mobilization—French call-up of reservists, manning the Maginot Line, canceling 40-hour week, authorized 60-hour week, calling up specific classes of reservists, policy on relief recipients refusing defense work—are provided with numbers and operational details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete measures, numbers or class descriptions, legal or decree authority, and immediate operational effects (e.g., who must report, penalties for noncompliance), to convey scope and seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contextual historical background
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatch places current events against prior milestones (reference to annexation of Austria and Sudetenland, 'September, 1938, Munich' and earlier treaties) to help readers understand continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly summarize relevant antecedent events and treaties to situate developments; avoid assuming reader familiarity and cite prior critical dates or agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use subheadings, boxed summaries, and numbered highlights for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece employs subheads (e.g., 'SILENT ON EUROPE', 'Further Steps Expected'), boxed lists and numbered 'These were:' style highlights summarizing main points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include short subheads and a concise numbered summary of primary facts or takeaways so readers can scan and grasp essentials quickly; ensure numbered points correspond to detailed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include color, ceremony, and human-interest details
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative passages describe banquets, receptions, crowds lining streets, what dignitaries wore and did (e.g., King George wearing scarlet uniform), and how spectators reacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add descriptive scene-setting and human details (crowd reactions, ceremonies) to enliven diplomatic reporting, while keeping such color accurate and relevant to the story's thrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on diplomatic negotiations, proposals, and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage outlines proposed conferences, who was being approached (Russia, France, Britain, Poland, Rumania, Turkey, Greece, Yugoslavia, Bulgaria), and the negotiators (Litvinov, Lord Halifax, Maxim Litvinov, Sir William Seeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name proposed initiatives, list proposed participants, identify envoys/negotiators, and note uncertainties or official characterizations (e.g., 'premature'); indicate what each proposal would change in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include maps/graphics and explanatory captions when helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes an illustrated 'MAP' and boxed map legends showing positions and proposed declarations (e.g., 'MAP 90' with caption about common policy of resistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide labeled maps or graphics that clarify geography and strategic lines referenced in the text; include a succinct caption explaining the map's relevance to the story.
